title: Release notes (2026-02): Quickstart templates v1 launch (RAG + Agents)
author: Nikhil Sharma
body:
h1. Quickstart templates v1 (2026-02)

This release introduces Redwood’s production-minded *Quickstart templates* to help developers go from “API key” to a working, observable application quickly—while avoiding unsafe patterns. The templates are designed to align with Redwood Hosted API and Redwood Console capabilities (token-level cost breakdowns, tracing, error taxonomy, routing/fallback posture) and to provide a clear path to Dedicated/Private deployment.

h2. What shipped

h3. 1) New template repository: redwood-quickstarts (v1)

We shipped three first-party templates with consistent structure and a stable “template contract” (env vars, telemetry schema, error codes, and SDK patterns).

*Template catalog (v1):*
* *RAG service + ingestion pipeline*
  * Python (FastAPI) and TypeScript (Node)
  * Ingestion worker + query API + vector store adapter layer
* *Agents (tool calling) template*
  * Tool allow-list, tool timeouts, output validation
  * Streaming-safe request handling patterns
* *Combined RAG + Agent template*
  * Retrieval exposed as a tool
  * Guardrails for prompt injection + tool misuse
  * Hooks for eval harness / regression checks

h3. 2) Observability pack (dashboards + alerts)

A minimal “observability pack” is now available for import so teams get baseline dashboards and non-noisy alerting out of the box.

*Includes:*
* Latency (p50/p95/p99) by route/model
* Token usage and cost attribution (by model/tenant/route)
* Error rate by error_class (client vs server, timeouts, upstream, validation, tool failures)
* 429 tracking (rate limit behavior and retry outcomes)
* Streaming disconnect indicators
* Burn-rate-style alert recommendations (with suppression guidance)

h3. 3) Telemetry contract v1 (standard)

Templates now emit a consistent set of:
* *Trace attributes* for request correlation (request_id, tenant_id, route, model, region, deployment_mode, template_name/version)
* *Structured log fields* that match traces and dashboards (correlation IDs + error taxonomy)
* *Metrics* for latency, retries, token usage, and tool execution

This enables consistent Console deep links from template logs/traces and reduces “works locally but invisible in prod” onboarding failures.

h3. 4) SDK improvements used by templates

* Python SDK: standardized retry/backoff defaults and streaming-safe timeouts used by templates.
* TypeScript SDK: improved error typing and clearer 429 handling; helpers for trace context propagation.

These changes were driven by the most common support issues seen in early dogfooding (streaming disconnects, missing timeouts, and confusing 429 behavior).

h3. 5) Deployment paths included in templates

Each template includes:
* Local run path (developer-first) with safe defaults
* Docker Compose dev stack (including health checks and resource limits)
* Minimal Kubernetes manifests (readiness/liveness probes, config/secrets patterns)

h3. 6) Documentation (docs-site integration)

We shipped landing pages and walkthroughs that:
* Help developers choose the right template (RAG vs agents vs combined)
* Explain safe defaults (timeouts/retries, PII handling guidance, tool allow-lists)
* Show how to enable observability (OpenTelemetry wiring + Console mapping)
* Provide a path to Dedicated/Private considerations

h2. Repository + doc links

* Repos:
  * redwood-quickstarts (templates): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-quickstarts
  * observability-pack (dashboards/alerts): https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-pack
  * redwood-examples (reference apps): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples

* Docs:
  * Quickstart templates landing page: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstarts
  * RAG template walkthrough: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstarts/rag
  * Agents template walkthrough: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstarts/agents
  * RAG + agent walkthrough: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstarts/rag-agents
  * Observability setup: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstarts/observability

h2. Versioning policy (templates + observability pack)

h3. Semantic versioning

*Templates* and the *observability pack* use *SemVer*.

* *MAJOR (X.0.0):* breaking changes to the template contract (env var names/behavior, telemetry contract changes, API surface changes in shared libs)
* *MINOR (0.Y.0):* new features/backends/templates, additive telemetry fields, new dashboards/panels
* *PATCH (0.0.Z):* bug fixes, security hardening, doc corrections, dependency bumps with no breaking behavior

h3. Template contract stability

For v1, the following are considered part of the stable contract:
* Env var names and precedence rules (e.g., environment overrides)
* Required telemetry fields and metric names
* Error taxonomy and error codes surfaced to callers
* Standard headers used for correlation (request ID + trace context)

h3. Compatibility matrix and pinning guidance

Templates pin compatible major versions of Redwood SDKs and list tested combinations.

*Policy:*
* Templates pin to *minimum* supported SDK versions and are tested in CI against a small matrix of SDK versions.
* For production deployments, we recommend pinning template and SDK versions together and upgrading intentionally (see “Upgrade steps”).

h3. Deprecations

* We will announce deprecations at least *30 days* before removing or renaming contract fields.
* Deprecated env vars (if any) will remain supported for at least *one MINOR release* and will log a warning at startup.

h2. Migration notes

h3. If you used older examples or ad-hoc starter code

If you are migrating from older Redwood examples (pre-templates) or internal snippets:

1) *Adopt the new env var contract*
* Move from free-form variable names to the standardized names documented in each template.
* Ensure you are not committing secrets; use .env only for local development and follow the secrets policy.

2) *Update retry/timeout behavior*
* Replace custom retry loops with the SDK helper defaults used by templates.
* Ensure streaming requests have explicit timeouts and disconnect handling.

3) *Align telemetry fields*
* Adopt the telemetry contract v1 field names so dashboards and Console views work without custom mapping.
* Ensure you pass through request_id and traceparent (or equivalent) from any edge proxy/gateway to the template service.

4) *Tool calling (agents)*
* Replace “open tool execution” with explicit allow-lists.
* Add tool timeouts and output schema validation (templates include this by default).

h3. Breaking behavior to watch for

* If you previously relied on “silent retries” for non-idempotent operations, review the idempotency guidance in the SDK docs.
* If you logged full prompts/responses for debugging, review PII guidance and the default logging behavior (templates avoid logging raw content by default).

h2. Upgrade steps (recommended)

When upgrading template versions:

1) Read the template CHANGELOG and identify contract-related changes (env vars, telemetry fields).
2) Upgrade templates and SDKs together (pin versions in your dependency manager).
3) Run smoke tests (the template repo includes an e2e path and telemetry validation).
4) Confirm dashboards still populate:
* request count, latency, token usage
* 429 rate + retry success
* error_class breakdown
5) For production: roll out with a canary and verify cost/latency deltas in Console.

h2. Known issues (launch window)

These are the top items to be aware of at launch (see the “Known issues” page for workarounds and updates):

* *Large document ingestion timeouts:* some customers may need to increase ingestion worker timeouts or chunking settings for large PDFs / long HTML.
* *Streaming behind certain proxies:* some proxy/load balancer defaults may buffer streaming responses unless explicitly configured.
* *429 confusion:* users unfamiliar with rate limits may misinterpret 429 as a hard failure; templates now show recommended backoff behavior, but docs callouts may still be needed.

h2. Ownership and support

*Primary owners:*
* DevEx: Alex Martinez (exec sponsor), Wei Chen (docs + templates), Dana Lo (TypeScript), Sabrina James (examples)
* SDK: Monica Patel (lead), Ibrahim Khan (TL)
* Observability: Logan Wright (platform), Sergio Costa (dashboards/alerts)
* Security review: Naomi Feldman, Marcus Lin
* SRE guardrails: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes

*Support workflow:*
* Bugs and papercuts: file in Linear under the Quickstart Templates project and tag *template* + *language*.
* Customer escalations: route via Support and link the relevant template version and logs/traces (include request_id).

h2. Next up (post-launch)

Planned follow-ups after v1:
* Expand backend support via adapter interfaces (prioritizing the most requested vector DB options).
* Improve eval harness integration and include a larger “minimum regression” prompt set.
* Harden Dedicated/Private deployment guidance (sizing, networking, audit logging, and telemetry retention patterns).

If you ship anything built off these templates, please keep the template version in your service metadata and include it in incident reports/escalations for faster triage.
